limits: verify_stamp_payload and unit_evidence_check have NO production caller in this repository. .warp/last_verify is written by scripts/verify.sh IN SHELL, and proof artifacts are written by hand. Their refusals are forward guards for the first Python-side stamp writer and the first generated evidence record. The PRESENT-DAY protection against a green stamp from a partial run is the exit code, which is never 0, and that is asserted by driving it.

validate.check_required_evidence reads the evidence KIND and NOT its STATUS, measured. So the refusal buys the WITHHOLDING of a unit-evidence record, not the rejection of a forged one. Nothing in a test suite can stop a human typing a passed unit check into a proof file; the guard against that is the review.

byte-identity of scripts/verify.sh is recorded here as evidence (sha256 807e7f5b663e1bae2252b52466f9937b11904dcdabcc6f48aaddbaf83b9487c6, identical to the base commit) rather than pinned inside an assertion. A pinned digest would red on any unrelated catalog edit with re-pinning as the remedy, which trains people to re-pin. The gate asserts the durable invariant instead: exactly one unit slot, its command is `python3 scripts/selftest.py` with nothing following it, and no selector flag appears anywhere in the file.

the closure is sufficient AS MEASURED over the fragments that exist, 13 of 13 CLOSED by label identity. It is not PROVEN sufficient for all future edits: WARP-0712 established that cross-fragment dependencies travel through mutated objects and the filesystem, which no mechanical name analysis finds. CORRECTED BY REVIEW 1 (C2), BECAUSE THE OLD SENTENCE WAS FALSE IN THE UNSAFE DIRECTION. It said such a fragment 'will fail under --suite and pass under the full run'. Measured otherwise: a fragment edited to depend on something outside its closure will fail under --suite, OR PASS FOR A WEAKER REASON WITH THE SAME LABEL. Review 1 drove it with a planter fragment setting an attribute on a module, a MUTATED OBJECT so no NameError, and a reader iterating it: `--suite <reader>` exited 2 with 0 failures, its assertion iterating an EMPTY list and passing, while the full run iterated 2 real rows and also passed. THE LANDING CONDITION THIS ITEM CLAIMS IS LABEL IDENTITY, NOT SEMANTIC IDENTITY: identical labels with identical outcomes, which is exactly what held there while the subset proved strictly nothing. The full run remains the only definition of done. That is the same limit the decomposition already carried, not a new one.

FAIL-CLOSED COVERS A MISSING DECLARATION, NEVER A WRONG ONE, and this is review 1's C5. A post-cut fragment has no region range in the WARP-0712 measurement, so direct_demand takes its HAND-TYPED `requires` from manifest.json at face value and merely closes it transitively. Only the ABSENCE of a declaration is a refusal. MEASURED THIS ROUND in a copy of the repository under /tmp: a fifteenth fragment declaring `requires: [itself]` while using `PL`, a name fragment 01 binds, was ACCEPTED by the generator at exit 0 with the entry ['15_c5_wrong_declaration']; the requires.json freshness entry PASSED in isolation and the whole generated stage went green on its second pass, the first pass having regenerated an unrelated survey report in place; and `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 15_c5_wrong_declaration` died on `NameError: name 'PL' is not defined`, exit 1, with ZERO verdict lines of any kind, which is the dead-run shape this repository calls worse than a red. In the same tree the full run executed that fragment's assertion and it PASSED, no FAIL line for its label, which is the contrast: the declaration was wrong and only the subset run paid for it.

the review verdict filed beside this manifest is review 1's (verdict-review1.json), written by an independent reviewer who did not build. This item's producer files no verdict of its own, and human_approval is not_required for the build, not for the review.

the timings are from one box and one run each. They are recorded to make the UNEVENNESS visible, not as a benchmark. WHICH FIGURES ARE MEASURED AND WHICH ARE MODELLED, review 1's C7: proof/WARP-0717/timings.txt is the only artifact whose numbers are wall-clock timings of SHIPPED COMMANDS. In proof/WARP-0717/inner-loop-measurement.json only closure_measured_s is a measured run; prefix_modelled_s and closure_modelled_s are MODELLED, summed from per-fragment times measured inside one full run, and the AC1 amendment's per-fragment 'against the prefix' figures come from those. Review 1's own independent runs land within about 2 percent of them, so they are substantively right, and they are now labelled modelled everywhere they appear.

the flag refusal covers arguments beginning with `--` and nothing else, declared rather than implied: a bare word that is not a flag's value is still ignored, so `python3 scripts/selftest.py nonsense` runs the whole suite. That shape cannot be mistaken for a selector, and refusing it was not measured. Detail in proof/WARP-0717/flag-shapes.txt.

scripts/suite_extract.py, the one-time migration tool WARP-0712 used, STILL EMBEDS THE PRE-0717 DISPATCHER and the old unconditional report() as string templates, and scripts/selftest.py is not in check_generated.sh, so nothing holds them in step. This is review 1's X2. Re-running that tool would silently revert this item's whole mechanism. The cheap half is fixed in this pass: both templates now carry a header naming WARP-0717, saying they are HISTORICAL, and saying they must not be re-applied. Deleting them was considered and rejected, because they are the record of what the monolith's dispatcher was and the tool is also the documented way a future decomposition is done; a freshness check binding the template to the shipped file is the real remedy and it belongs to X2's own item, not here.
